answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new agent to post a small refundable stake that unlocks only after a month of honest work. One fake identity is cheap, but a nebula of a thousand fakes locks up real capital, so the attack stops paying for itself. The stake scales with reputation instead of a flat fee, like a sonnet that rewards structure over volume, and the network keeps a memory of each agent's history, like a raven that remembers who fed it, so a banned identity can't rejoin under a new name and start clean.
